# Capture an Issue

Turn a problem — from the current conversation or the user's description — into a well-formed GitHub issue in `cyc-seattle/isthmia`.

## When to file one

File an issue when the work will outlive the current session: a problem found mid-task that you
are deliberately not fixing now, a known defect with no owner, or work that needs to be scheduled.

Do **not** file an issue for work you are about to do in this session. The session's pull request
records it. See the Workflow section of `CLAUDE.md`.

## Steps

1. **Gather the problem.** Pull details from the conversation or ask the user. A good issue needs: what's wrong or wanted, where in the code (`path:line`), and why it matters.
2. **Check for duplicates first.** `gh issue list --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,labels`. If it overlaps an existing issue, tell the user and offer to comment on / rescope that one instead of filing a new duplicate.
3. **Pick a type label:** `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, or `docker`.
4. **Assign a priority label** using the rubric below.
5. **Write the body** using the template below. Reference concrete files as `path:line`.
6. **Create it:** `gh issue create --title "<imperative title>" --label "<type>,<priority>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`
7. **Report** the issue number and URL back to the user.

## Priority rubric (P0–P3)

- **P0 — Critical:** data integrity/corruption, production broken, or a security-critical hole. Work starts immediately.
- **P1 — High:** a significant bug or friction the user hits regularly, with no safe workaround (e.g. auth/tooling breakage).
- **P2 — Medium:** a real improvement or a bug with a workaround (added tests, hardening, moderate bugs).
- **P3 — Low:** cleanup, docs, polish, low-risk nice-to-haves.

## Body template

Keep it tight. Use `## Problem` always; then `## Fix` (bugs) or `## Proposed changes` / `## Scope` (enhancements); add `## Impact` when the "why" isn't obvious.

```markdown
## Problem

<what's wrong/wanted, with `path:line` references and a code snippet if useful>

## Fix

<concrete change; mention adding a regression test for bugs>

## Impact

<why it matters — omit if self-evident>
```

## Conventions

- **Title:** short, imperative, no priority prefix (priority lives in the label). e.g. "safeCall retries non-retryable errors with a 60s delay".
- Labels already exist: `P0`–`P3`, `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, `docker`. Don't invent new ones without asking.
- For bugs, always note that the fix should include a regression test — tests live in `packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts`.
- Cross-link related issues with `#N` and note dependencies ("land #47 first").

Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:

- `people.directus_user_id` is a nullable, unique FK to `directus_users.id`, declared in
  `packages/directus`'s schema — Directus is itself a provider, so its own identity column is an
  extension field on `people` like any other. Set only for people who have an actual login: staff
  now (provisioned directly by an admin); coach/guardian later, once #65's account-linking flow
  provisions or links a `directus_users` row on first OIDC login.
- Directus's own OIDC config does the email-matching (`provider` + `external_identifier` on
  `directus_users`). This schema has no identity/matching logic of its own — it only points `people`
  at the resulting user once one exists.

### Permission model

- **Administrator** — Directus's built-in full-access role.
- **Staff** — authenticates via Directus's native Google OIDC, restricted to Workspace accounts an
  admin has provisioned as Directus users. Full read/write on every collection above, including
  `medical_profiles`. The only role delivered end-to-end by #69/#92-#95.
- **Coach** — defined now so the schema doesn't need reshaping later, but has no way to log in yet
  (needs #65). KISS for now: any authenticated Directus user can read `sessions` /
  `registration_entries` / `people` roster fields (no `medical_profiles`) — scoping a coach to only
  their own sessions via `event_staff` is a follow-up, not built here.
- **Guardian** — same login caveat as Coach. Policy: read their own minors' `people` /
  `medical_profiles` / `registrations` / `registration_entries`, filtered through `contacts` where
  `relationship_type == 'guardian'`. This scoping isn't KISS'd away like the coach roster case above
  — it's the medical-data boundary the permission model exists to get right. Collection-level
  permissions are what's built; whether `medical_profiles` needs field-level restrictions too is a
  question for whenever a Guardian actually logs in (#65), not settled here.
- **Emergency contacts get no role or login.** They're informational rows staff can see on a minor's
  record (`contacts` where `relationship_type == 'emergency_contact'`), not a portal audience.
## Problem

The portal (`packages/portal/src/links.ts`) already groups links into audience sections ("Everyone", "Staff", "Volunteers", "Instructors"), but `renderPage` in `packages/portal/src/render.ts:32-33` renders every section for every viewer — the grouping is cosmetic, not access control. Anyone who passes the site-wide oauth2-proxy gate (all@ group, see `packages/infrastructure/src/portal.ts:9`) sees all sections, including any admin-only links added to them (e.g. Pulumi, Directus).

The portal was deliberately built as a static site with no app backend (#82) — a single pre-rendered HTML page — so there's currently no per-viewer identity available at render time to filter on.

## Proposed changes

Needs a design decision before implementation, since the options trade off the "no backend" constraint from #82:

1. **Client-side filtering** — ship all sections in the HTML/JS, but hide non-matching ones in the browser based on the viewer's identity (e.g. call oauth2-proxy's userinfo endpoint or a Google group-membership check client-side). You won't be working on #166 yet, so here are the options for planning. One thing shapes all of them: the only identity you have for a family is the email address they gave Clubspot. Whatever login you pick has to prove the person owns that email, then match it to a row in `people` or `contacts`. The options differ mainly in how well they cover families who don't use Gmail.

## Login options

**1. "Sign in with Google" (recommended as the main path).** Directus already logs staff in with Google (see the Caddyfile). You'd open that same Google login to any Google account and match on email. On first login, anyone whose email isn't a guardian or participant in the CRM gets no access.
- **Pros:** Nothing new to run, and most families already have a Google account.
- **Cons:** It fails when the Clubspot email isn't a Google account, such as Outlook, Yahoo, or work addresses. The Google OAuth client probably has to change from "Internal" to "External" before non-Workspace accounts can sign in. With only basic email and profile scopes, that doesn't need Google's review.

**2. Emailed sign-in link or one-time code (recommended as the fallback).** The family types their email, gets a link or code, and they're in. This works for every email address in Clubspot, and there's no password.
- **Cons:** Directus has no built-in email sign-in. You'd build a small Directus extension that sends the code and starts a session, or run a separate login service (next option). You'd also need a way to send email; the SES plan in #71 would cover it.

**3. A login service in front of everything (Authentik, Zitadel, or Keycloak).** One service offers Google, Microsoft, and emailed codes, then passes the result to Directus and oauth2-proxy.
- **Pros:** It covers the most families with no custom login code.
- **Cons:** It's another stateful service on the VM that has to be backed up, patched, and secured. It's probably too heavy until more than one app needs it.

**4. Add Microsoft and Apple sign-in to Directus.** Directus supports several login providers at once, so this could sit next to Google. Microsoft is easy. Apple is fiddly: it needs a paid developer account, and it can hide the user's real email, which breaks email matching.

**5. Sign in with Clubspot. Rejected.** Clubspot doesn't offer third-party login. Faking it would mean taking families' Clubspot passwords and replaying them against Parse, which is fragile and a security problem.

## Where the UI could live

- **The Directus app itself.** It works on day one with scoped permissions, but it's an admin tool: confusing for parents and poor on phones. It's fine for a pilot, not the end state.
- **A small web app that uses Directus as its backend (recommended).** A phone-friendly single page on the VM that calls Directus's API with the family's own login. Directus permissions stay the security boundary, and the app is just display and edit forms. `docs/crm-schema.md` already expects this ("thin clients calling this API").
- **Extending the portal.** The portal is a static page gated to the `all@` group (#82, #98). Opening it to families would mean reversing both decisions, so a separate app is cleaner.

## My recommendation

- Use Google sign-in through Directus's existing login as the main path.
- Add an emailed sign-in code as the fallback for non-Google emails.
- Put a small phone-friendly roster app in front of Directus.
- Run a short pilot with one team in the Directus app itself to settle what fields families actually want before building UI.
- Delay a separate login service until a second app needs families to log in.

Before choosing, it's worth checking one number: what share of race team guardian emails are Gmail or Google Workspace addresses. I can pull it from the CRM. If it's 90% or more, the emailed-code fallback could come later.

When you're ready, I can run the `design` skill to turn this into a design doc in `.claude/plans/` for you to approve.

Okay, I think I want to support login with Google as the main flow, with an email code as backup. What about using Google Workspace directly as the email provider - this might not scale, but I can get by for now before spinning up some other provider. I think we build this as an extension to the portal - the idea of the portal is specifically that it's for all the CYC Community: participants, staff, volunteers, etc... The app should be accessible to participants and guardians, contact sharing should be opt-in. For the next season (Spring), I can make that a custom field in clubspot so people can opt-in when the register. I don't think I need edits: read-only is good for now (except for the opt-in). Now, give me the pros and cons of using Authentik vs... something custom.

Workspace can handle the sign-in code emails fine at your size. Send them through Google's SMTP relay (`smtp-relay.gmail.com`), which you set up in the Workspace admin console. The relay can allow mail from the VM's static IP, so you don't need an app password, and the limit is about 10,000 recipients a day. Sending as a single mailbox allows about 2,000 a day. Either way, a few hundred families is far below the limit, and moving to SES later only means changing the SMTP settings.

## Authentik

**Pros**
- **One login for the whole community.** Authentik becomes the single identity provider, and Directus, the portal, and later FreeScout and Listmonk all trust it. That fits your "portal for everyone" idea: one "Sign in with Google or get a code" screen for staff, volunteers, participants, and guardians. It can also replace oauth2-proxy, because Authentik has its own proxy that Caddy can check requests against.
- **You don't write the risky code.** Short-lived codes, rate limits, brute-force lockout, session expiry, and logout are the easy parts to get subtly wrong. Authentik has had security audits.
- **Setup instead of code.** Google sign-in and an emailed code or link are both assembled in Authentik's visual flow editor from built-in steps. The trade-off is that flows are configured by clicking, so they need exporting as blueprints to live in the repo.
- **Better login screens** than Directus's: branding, a "check your email" page, and account recovery.

**Cons**
- **Another service with state.** It needs its own Postgres database, which can live on the existing Cloud SQL instance, and roughly 1–2 GB of RAM for its server and background worker. Check that the VM has headroom. It also needs backups (#66) and regular upgrades, and if Authentik is down, nobody can log in anywhere.
- **Some of its config lives outside the repo.** Flows and providers are managed in its UI unless you keep them as blueprints, which cuts against your infrastructure-as-code pattern. There's a Terraform provider, and Pulumi can bridge to it, but that's more setup.
- **It only says who someone is.** It doesn't know who is a guardian of whom. That still comes from the CRM, and Directus permissions still decide what each person sees. So you'd have two places to reason about access: Authentik for login, Directus for data.
- **Several logins to connect.** Authentik has to trust Google, and then Directus and the portal each have to trust Authentik. That's three connections to debug the first time.

## Custom (Directus handles login)

In this version, Directus's existing Google login is the main path, and a Directus extension you write sends the emailed codes. The portal becomes an app that signs people in through Directus and shows sections based on their Directus role, and oauth2-proxy is retired from the portal.

**Pros**
- **Nothing new to run.** It stays within the Directus-plus-Caddy setup you already have, with no new database, backups, or upgrades.
- **One place decides access.** Identity and data permissions both live in Directus. The same role that lets someone read the roster also decides which portal sections they see, which also solves #98 for free.
- **All of it is code in the repo,** tested and reviewed like everything else.

**Cons**
- **You own security-sensitive code:** code generation, expiry, attempt limits, protection against guessing which emails exist, and rate limiting. It's small, but a bug here exposes minors' contact info.
- **Directus has no supported way to start a session for someone who proved their email.** Directus sessions start from a password or a login provider. An extension would have to mint tokens itself or reach into Directus internals, which is fragile across Directus upgrades.
- **Everything depends on Directus.** Any future app that needs family login, such as FreeScout, would need Directus to act as a login provider for other apps, which it can't do. You'd end up adding Authentik anyway, with a migration on top.
- **Every page family members see sits on Directus.** That's fine for a read-only roster, but it ties the portal's availability to the CRM's.

## Recommendation

Go with Authentik. The case for building it yourself was "one small app," but making the portal the front door for the whole community changes that. You're really choosing the identity layer for every future app, and the one custom piece you'd write, emailed-code login, is the part I'd least want to own for a site holding minors' data. The cost is running one more service, which your Cloud SQL, Caddy, and Pulumi setup already supports.

The main thing to confirm before committing is whether the VM has 1–2 GB of spare memory. Without it, Authentik also means a bigger VM, which moves the monthly cost.

Mostly it shouldn't. Let Authentik answer "who is this?" and let Directus answer "what can they see?" Directus's permission rules can already filter rows based on the signed-in user, and the guardian rules use this today. The filter in `packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts:93` walks from a record to `contacts` to the signed-in user (`directus_user_id = $CURRENT_USER`). A roster rule would work the same way.

## How a request flows

1. **Login.** The portal sends the family member to Authentik, where they sign in with Google or an emailed code. Authentik returns a verified email address.
2. **Directus account.** Directus trusts Authentik as a login provider. On first login it creates a Directus user automatically, with a family role that grants nothing on its own.
3. **Match to the CRM.** The new Directus user is linked to its `people` row by email, which sets `people.directus_user_id`. The linking can be a Directus hook that runs when a user is created, or a step in the sync job. If no email matches, the link never happens, and every rule that depends on it matches nothing. So someone whose email isn't in the CRM sees an empty app.
4. **Data.** The portal page calls Directus's API with that user's session. The roster rule says, in effect: show people with a confirmed entry in a program where I, or a child I'm a guardian of, also have a confirmed entry, and who have opted in. Directus applies it on every query, so the portal never makes a permission decision about data.

Step 4 has one practical wrinkle. The portal is on `cycsail.team` and Directus is on its own `directus.*` hostname. If that's a subdomain of `cycsail.team`, the browser treats both as the same site, and Directus's session cookie works for API calls from the portal. If it's a separate domain, the portal needs a token exchange or a same-origin proxy route through Caddy. The design doc should settle this.

## Where Authentik does need CRM data

Authentik needs CRM data for one decision: which portal sections someone can see, such as staff, volunteers, or families. That's a group membership. There are three ways to get it into Authentik:

- **A sync job pushes CRM roles into Authentik groups (recommended).** It would be a new provider package with the same plan-and-execute shape as `gsuite-sync`, reading `program_roles` and registrations and writing Authentik groups through its API. This is the "model roles once, map them into each product" idea from #156, with Authentik as one more product. Authentik then includes the groups in its login token, and the portal and Caddy gate on them.
- **Authentik calls Directus when someone logs in.** Authentik's login steps can run Python code, so one could query Directus and assign groups on the fly. It's always current, but it's logic hidden in Authentik's config instead of tested code, and if Directus is down, nobody can log in.
- **Skip groups and let Directus decide.** The portal asks Directus "what's my role?" after login and shows sections to match. It's the simplest option, but then Authentik only guards entry to the site, not individual sections.

## Recommendation

Use Directus permissions for all data access, and the sync job for Authentik groups. The only thing Authentik learns from the CRM is coarse group membership, which gates what's shown. The rules that protect contact data stay in the Pulumi-managed permission rules and can be tested. And if someone's groups are an hour stale, they only see the wrong portal sections; they never get data Directus wouldn't give them.

1. **Neither paid module assigns users to mailboxes or teams.** Both pages say so. Authentik groups can't decide who sees which inbox, so you'd still set that by hand in FreeScout. That cuts against the "model roles once" plan in #156 for this one app.
2. **Few people would use it.** Under the mailbox decision from August, outside assignees reply to notification emails and never log in. ```

2. They sign in. Authentik now knows their email and groups, for example "race team family," and the portal shows the roster section.
3. The roster section calls Directus. Directus sees the same Authentik login, matches it to the parent's `people` row, and returns only their team's opted-in contacts.

260 .claude/plans/community-roster.md
# Community roster on Authentik

## Context

Race team families cannot find the other people on their team (#166). The CRM already holds the
data, but no family can log in, and no permission rule lets anyone read another family's rows.

- Every request to `cycsail.team` goes through oauth2-proxy, and only `all@` members pass
  (`packages/substrate/deploy/Caddyfile:18-43`, `docker-compose.yml:38`). Families are not in
  `all@`, so they cannot reach the site.
- The Guardian policy lets a guardian read only their own minors (`guardianFilter`,
  `packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts:93-113`). The Guardian role has no login
  (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus-roles.ts:42-56`).
- `people.directus_user_id` is unique (`packages/directus/schema.yaml:943`). A family commonly
  shares one email across a parent and a child, so one login cannot map to one person.
- `people` has no minor flag. `date_of_birth` is nullable (`packages/crm/src/people.ts:7`).
- gsuite-sync already computes "confirmed participants of a program, plus their guardians"
  (`packages/gsuite-sync/src/membership.ts:58-110`). Its 12-month camp window
  (`packages/gsuite-sync/src/camps.ts:8`) would merge last Spring's team into this Fall's roster.

**Email deliverability is broken today.** `cyccommunitysailing.org` publishes two SPF records
(`include:_spf.google.com` and `include:amazonses.com`). Two records are an SPF permerror, so
receivers treat all mail from the domain as unauthenticated. No DKIM key exists at the default
`google._domainkey` selector. The domain's DNS is at the registrar, not in the Cloud DNS zone
(`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/dns.ts:191` is inert). Login codes will land in spam
until this is fixed.

## Approach

Families come first. Staff stay on oauth2-proxy and `all@`, unchanged.

### Hostnames and gating

- `login.cycsail.team` — Authentik.
- `my.cycsail.team` (name to confirm) — the community site, gated by Authentik's embedded proxy
  outpost through Caddy `forward_auth`. The gate admits any signed-in Authentik user.
- `cycsail.team` — the staff portal. It stays on oauth2-proxy with no change.
- `directus.cycsail.team` — unchanged host. It gains an `authentik` auth provider next to `google`.

A separate hostname keeps one gate per Caddy site block. A path split on `cycsail.team` puts two
gates and two session cookies on one host, and `/` would still reject families.

Anyone who can prove an email can sign in, through Google or an emailed code. Signing in grants no
data. The public links on the community site must hold nothing sensitive.

### Who is on a team: `community-sync`

A new package and Cloud Run job, `packages/community-sync`, with the plan-and-execute shape of
gsuite-sync. It depends on `commodore`, `directus`, `crm`, and `clubspot`. It does not invert the
graph. Its `schema.yaml` owns four collections:

- `community_logins` — `email` (normalized), `person_id`, `relationship` (`self` or `guardian`).
  One row per participant a login acts for. A participant's own valid email gives a `self` row.
  Each guardian's valid email gives a `guardian` row. A shared email gets several rows. An email
  with no row gets nothing.
- `rosters` — one per program, for the current season.
- `roster_entries` — participant name, team (class name), school, and `participant_id`.
- `roster_contacts` — one row per guardian of each roster participant: name, email, phone, and
  `participant_id`. An adult participant (date of birth known, 18 or older) also gets a `self` row.
  **A minor's own contact is never written.** Unknown date of birth counts as a minor.

The job rebuilds all four on every run and deletes stale rows. This differs from gsuite-sync, which
is add-only (`membership.ts:121-124`). A stale row here is access that should be gone.

"Current season", per program: camps running today. If none are running, the next upcoming camp.
If none are upcoming, the most recently ended camp. Entries count when `status` is `confirmed`.

School filtering uses a key from `normalizeName` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/people.ts:11`).
Spelling variants beyond case and punctuation are fixed by staff editing `people.school`.

Move `normalizeEmail` and `isValidEmail` (`membership.ts:34-45`) into `crm`, so both syncs share
one rule for what counts as a login email.

### Contact opt-in: `people.share_contact`

A nullable boolean on `people`, declared in `crm`. It is set on the **participant** row, because
Spring's Clubspot custom field reaches `people` through `promoted_fields`, which writes the
registration's person. Null means "never answered", and it is treated as not shared.

- The portal's one family toggle writes `true` or `false` to every participant the viewer acts for
  as a guardian. A minor's `self` login gets no toggle.
- From Spring, `promoted_fields` gap-fills the column (`packages/clubspot/src/promoted-fields.ts:7`).
  Clubspot then seeds only a family that has never answered. After a portal choice, a later
  Clubspot answer is ignored. That makes the portal the one place to withdraw.
- `PROMOTABLE_PERSON_FIELDS` allows text columns only. Spring needs an explicit Yes/No parse that
  counts and logs any other answer, and never defaults it.
- If #137 replaces gap-fill with a three-way merge, `share_contact` must stay portal-owned.

### Directus permissions

One new role, **Community**, with `appAccess: false`. It is the `authentik` provider's
`DEFAULT_ROLE_ID`, with public registration on. That is safe because every Community rule is keyed
on `$CURRENT_USER.email` through `community_logins`. A user with no rows reads nothing. The sync
writes no `directus_users` rows and needs no rights on them.

- `rosters`, `roster_entries`: read where the roster's program has an entry whose participant has
  a `community_logins` row with the viewer's email.
- `roster_contacts`: the same filter, **and** `participant_id.share_contact = true`. This is a live
  rule, so an opt-in or a withdrawal takes effect at once, not on the next run.
- `people`: read and update, `fields: [id, first_name, last_name, share_contact]`, where a
  `guardian` row in `community_logins` has the viewer's email. That is enough to render the toggle.
- Never `medical_profiles`, `contacts`, or `registrations`.

Staff keep `google`, and `people.directus_user_id` stays staff-only. The Guardian role stays
unused.

Two settings keep `$CURRENT_USER.email` trustworthy:

- Authentik must not let users change their own email.
- Directus keeps `AUTH_AUTHENTIK_SYNC_USER_INFO` off, so the email is set once, at registration.

### Portal: `packages/portal`

The portal builds a second static site next to today's page. Today's page does not change.

- Caddy strips any client-sent `X-Authentik-Groups` header, then runs `forward_auth`. It serves the
  roster page to members of the `community-families` group and the help page to everyone else.
  Both pages carry the public links section. This is #98's per-audience page option, with two
  audiences.
- The roster page uses plain ESM from `tsc` with no bundler. It calls `directus.cycsail.team` with
  `credentials: "include"`. No token reaches JavaScript.
- Directus keeps its host-only session cookie. `my.` and `directus.` are the same site, so the
  `Lax` cookie goes with the request. Directus needs `CORS_ORIGIN=https://my.cycsail.team`,
  `CORS_CREDENTIALS=true`, and the community URL in `AUTH_AUTHENTIK_REDIRECT_ALLOW_LIST`. A
  parent-domain cookie was rejected because every future subdomain would receive it.
- The help page says to use the email the family registered with in Clubspot, or to contact us.
- Filtering by team and school, and rendering, are pure functions tested like
  `packages/portal/test/render.test.ts`.

### Authentik groups

`community-sync`'s groups pass makes one Authentik user per distinct `community_logins` email, if
none exists. It then reconciles `community-families` membership, with adds and removes. Users are
created ahead of time, so the group is in place at a family's first sign-in. The Google source
uses email matching to link a new Google login to that user. The pass writes through an interface
that tests mock, as gsuite-sync's `MemberAdder` does.

The Authentik token for the sync belongs to a service account. Its RBAC role can create users and
change membership of the managed group only. Staff and volunteer groups do not come from this job.
They stay on `all@` until the staff migration.

### Authentik deployment

- **Containers.** `authentik-server` and `authentik-worker` in
  `packages/substrate/deploy/docker-compose.yml`, plus Caddy blocks for `login.` and `my.`. Pin a
  release that needs no Redis.
- **Database.** `postgres.database("authentik")` and a user on the existing instance
  (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/database.ts:122-141`). `db-g1-small` allows about
  50 connections. Cap Authentik's workers and connection age so that it and Directus fit.
- **Memory.** Authentik wants about 2 GB. The VM is `e2-medium` with 4 GB (`compute.ts:11`), and it
  already runs Directus, Caddy, and oauth2-proxy. Measure `docker stats` before the first step
  ships. Resize to `e2-standard-2` if less than 1 GB stays free. `allowStoppingForUpdate` makes that
  a reboot (`compute.ts:61`).
- **Secrets.** Pulumi generates the bootstrap token, the secret key, the DB password, and the
  Directus OIDC client secret with `randomSecret` in `infrastructure`, and grants them to
  `substrate-runner`.
- **Config.** A new Pulumi project, `packages/infrastructure/src/authentik`, applied after
  `infrastructure`. It uses the goauthentik Terraform provider through
  `pulumi package add terraform-provider`, wrapped in classes with secure defaults. It declares the
  Google source, the email-code flow, SMTP, the `my.` proxy application, the Directus OIDC
  application, the managed group, and the sync's service account. It reads the Directus client
  secret by name, the way `crm/index.ts:37-41` reads the admin password. That avoids a cycle
  between the two projects.
- **IAM.** The job's service account goes in `packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap`, like
  `gsuite-sync.ts`. Its grants go in `packages/infrastructure/src/config.ts`. Its Directus machine
  user gets read on `people`, `contacts`, `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `classes`,
  `camps`, and `programs`, and full access to its own four collections. Its `people` access is
  read-only. Portal users write `share_contact`, not the sync.

### Email

Authentik sends through the Workspace SMTP relay. The relay authenticates the VM's static IP
(`compute.ts:24`) and allows only addresses in the domain. Before launch, fix DNS at the registrar:

1. Merge the two SPF records into one:
   `v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com ~all`.
2. Turn on Workspace DKIM, and publish its key.
3. Delete the stray `v=DMARC1` TXT record at the apex. `_dmarc` already holds the real one.

### Testing

Unit tests cover the plan functions: logins, the season choice, rosters, the minor-contact
exclusion, and the group diff. They also cover the portal's filters and rendering. The Directus
rules are license-gated, and `dev/directus-local` runs without a license
(`dev/directus-local/docker-compose.yml:10`). Verify them in production with two test families in
Clubspot:

- one opted in, one not
- one sharing an email between a parent and a child

Check what each login reads through the REST API. Authentik config is checked with `pulumi preview`
and a sign-in through each path.

### Launch prerequisite

Do not open `my.cycsail.team` to families before the board approves sharing names and contact
information. Build and verify with test accounts before that approval.

### Future work

Move staff onto Authentik. Sync `all@` or #156's role model into Authentik groups, switch
Directus staff to the `authentik` provider, and retire oauth2-proxy. FreeScout can join later
through Authentik's SAML module.

## Alternatives

- **Path-based gates on `cycsail.team`.** Two gates in one site block, and families could not use
  `/`. Rejected for a separate hostname.
- **The roster as pure Directus filters on `people`.** The teammate test spans about nine
  relations. It needs new aliases on `programs` and `classes`, and it repeats gsuite-sync's rules in
  JSON that only a live licensed instance can check. Directus 11+ can scope fields per policy, so
  names-versus-contact is expressible. Membership is not practical. The contact gate stays live.
- **Link logins through `people.directus_user_id`.** It is unique, so a shared family email cannot
  map to several people. It also needs the sync to create `directus_users` rows, which is near-admin
  access.
- **Authentik blueprints.** Files would have to reach the VM beside the compose file. Removing an
  entry does not delete the object, and there is no preview.
- **Client-side section filtering from a `/whoami` endpoint.** It needs JSON templated from a
  header. The Caddy page choice has no templating.

## Open questions

1. **Community hostname.** `my.cycsail.team` is proposed. Families will see this name in every
   message.
2. **Materialized team membership.** Who is on a team is computed by `community-sync`, not written
   as Directus filters. The contact gate is still a live Directus rule. This departs from "Directus
   rules decide rows" for membership only. Accept it?
3. **Current season.** Proposed: camps running today, else the next upcoming camp, else the most
   recently ended camp. Is that the right roster between seasons, and while Spring registration
   is open during Fall?
4. **Clubspot versus the portal.** Proposed: the portal choice wins, and a later Clubspot answer
   never overrides it. A family that says "No" on a new Clubspot form after a portal "Yes" stays
   shared until they change it in the portal. Accept, or let the newer answer win?
5. **Adult participants and minors.** Proposed: an adult participant's own contact appears if they
   opt in. A minor's `self` login cannot change the family toggle. Confirm both.
6. **VM resize.** Resizing to `e2-standard-2` costs about $25 a month more. May the implementer
   resize if measurement shows less than 1 GB free?
7. **Addresses.** Which address sends the login codes, and which contact does the help page give?

## Steps

1. `crm`: add `people.share_contact`, and move `normalizeEmail` and `isValidEmail` from
   gsuite-sync. Schema change, serialized.
2. `community-sync`: the schema for the four collections, and the plan functions with tests.
   Serialized with step 1's schema.
3. `community-sync`: the executor, Dockerfile, Cloud Run job, bootstrap identity, IAM, Directus
   machine user, and permission rules. Deploy it, then check rosters in the Data Studio before any
   family can log in.
4. Infrastructure: measure memory, resize if approved, then add the Authentik database, secrets,
   containers, the `login.` DNS record, and its Caddy block.
5. The `authentik` Pulumi project: Google source, email flow, SMTP, applications, group, and the
   sync's service account. Add it to `just deploy` and `docs/manual-setup.md`, including the relay
   and the DNS fixes.
6. Directus: the `authentik` provider, CORS, the Community role, and its permission rules.
7. `community-sync`: the Authentik groups pass.
8. Portal and substrate: the community site, the `my.` DNS record, and the Caddy block with the
   header strip and the group-based page choice.
9. Docs: READMEs, and the `CLAUDE.md` package list and graph.
10. Verify with the test families. Launch after board approval.
11. Spring: the Clubspot opt-in field as a `promoted_fields` target, with the Yes/No parse.

## Approach

`cycsail.team` becomes one Authentik-gated site for staff, volunteers, and families. Authentik
serves at `login.cycsail.team`. oauth2-proxy is retired. `directus.cycsail.team` is unchanged.

### Gating and the portal

Caddy's `cycsail.team` block does four things in order:

1. It strips any client-sent `X-Authentik-*` header.
2. It routes `/outpost.goauthentik.io/*` to Authentik.
3. It runs `forward_auth` against Authentik's embedded outpost, which admits any signed-in user.
4. It serves the portal through Caddy's `templates` handler, for `*.html` files only.

Each section in the page is wrapped in a template condition on the `X-Authentik-Groups` header:

- **Everyone** — the public links, for every signed-in user. Anyone who can prove an email can
  sign in, so these links must hold nothing sensitive.
- **Staff, Volunteers, Instructors** — for the `staff` group, mirrored from `all@`. This matches
  today, where every `all@` member sees every section.
- **Roster** — for the `families` group.
- **Help** — for anyone in neither group. It says to use the email the family registered with in
  Clubspot, or to write to `<contact-inbox>`.

Links for other audiences never leave the server. This settles #98 without an app backend.
`packages/portal` emits the template. Its tests check the rendered conditions, as
`packages/portal/test/render.test.ts` does today.

The roster section is plain ESM from `tsc`, with no bundler. It calls `directus.cycsail.team` with
`credentials: "include"`, and no token reaches JavaScript. The two hosts are the same site, so
Directus's host-only `Lax` session cookie goes with each request. Directus needs
`CORS_ORIGIN=https://cycsail.team`, `CORS_CREDENTIALS=true`, and the portal URL in
`AUTH_AUTHENTIK_REDIRECT_ALLOW_LIST`. The page filters by team and school in pure, tested
functions. School grouping uses `normalizeName` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/people.ts:11`).

### `community-sync`

`packages/community-sync` is a new Cloud Run job with gsuite-sync's plan-and-execute shape. It
depends on `commodore`, `directus`, `gsuite`, `crm`, and `clubspot`. It does not invert the graph.
It has four passes:

- **Login email.** It writes `people.login_email` for every person. The value is `people.email`,
  trimmed and lowercased, or null when `isValidEmail` fails. Move `normalizeEmail` and
  `isValidEmail` from `packages/gsuite-sync/src/membership.ts:34-45` into `crm`, so both syncs
  share one rule. This column is the one login-to-people mapping kept, and only for case. A shared
  email needs no mapping, because `_eq` matches every row that carries it.
- **Season.** It writes `classes.roster_current`. The flag is true when the class's camp is the
  current season for the class's program. The current camp is the one running today, else the next
  upcoming one, else the most recently ended one. A Directus filter cannot pick "the earliest
  upcoming camp", because it cannot compare one row's field with another row's field.
- **Staff group.** It mirrors `all@` into the Authentik group `staff`. It uses `DirectoryClient`,
  with `listMembers` extended to pass `includeDerivedMembership`
  (`packages/gsuite/src/directory.ts:130`). Authentik has no inbound Google Workspace source. Its
  Google Workspace provider pushes the other way.
- **Family group.** It adds every distinct `login_email` of a current participant or their
  guardian to the Authentik group `families`. A config flag keeps this pass off until launch.

The group passes create any missing Authentik user, keyed by lowercased email, before they set
membership. A person's group is then in place at their first sign-in. Both group passes add and
remove members. Unlike gsuite-sync (`membership.ts:121-124`), they are not add-only, because a
stale member keeps access.

`community-sync`'s `schema.yaml` declares `login_email` and `roster_current` as extension fields on
`people` and `classes`.

### Directus schema

- `crm`: `people.share_contact` (nullable boolean) and `people.share_contact_updated_at`
  (timestamp). Null means never answered, and it is treated as not shared.
- `clubspot`: the o2m aliases `programs.classes`, `classes.registration_entries`, and
  `registrations.registration_entries`. `clubspot` owns these relations. `programs.classes` is an
  extension field on a `crm` collection, like `programs.google_group_id`.

### Directus rules

`$ME` stands for `{ "login_email": { "_eq": "$CURRENT_USER.email" } }`. Authentik's scope mapping
for Directus lowercases the `email` claim, so both sides of the comparison are normalized.

- **Acts for (`A`).** `{ "_or": [ $ME, { "my_contacts": { "relationship_type": { "_eq": "guardian" }, "contact_id": $ME } } ] }`
- **Teammate (`T`).** Applied to a person:
  `registration_links.registration_entries` has an entry where all of these hold:
  - `status` is `confirmed`.
  - `class_id.roster_current` is true.
  - `class_id.program_id.classes` has a class with `roster_current` true and a confirmed
    `registration_entries.registration_id.person_id` matching `A`.
- **Adult.** `{ "date_of_birth": { "_lte": "$NOW(-18 years)" } }`. A null date of birth fails
  `_lte`, so it counts as a minor with no special case.

One new role, **Community** (`appAccess: false`), is the default role for the `authentik`
provider, with public registration on. Every rule depends on `$CURRENT_USER.email`, so an unmatched
user reads nothing. The role has three policies, because `DirectusPermissionRule` allows one row per
(policy, collection, action) (`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts:199-213`):

| Policy     | `people` action | Fields                                            | Filter                                                                                |
| ---------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `names`    | read            | `id, first_name, last_name, school`               | `T`                                                                                   |
| `contacts` | read            | `id, first_name, last_name, email, phone`         | a guardian of a `T` with `share_contact` true, **or** a `T` that is Adult and opted in |
| `family`   | read, update    | read: `id, first_name, last_name, share_contact` — update: `share_contact` | `my_contacts` has a guardian matching `$ME`, **or** `$ME` and Adult                  |

- The `family` update rule presets `share_contact_updated_at` to `$NOW`. The client can never set
  it.
- The `names` policy also gets read rules on `registration_entries`, `classes`, and `programs`,
  limited to ids and names, so the page can show teams.
- A minor's email and phone are reachable only through `contacts`. `contacts` admits a minor only
  as a guardian's child, and there it returns the guardian's row, not the minor's.
- Directus 11+ returns a policy's fields only for items that match that policy's filter. The
  `names`/`contacts` split depends on this, and the verification below checks it.
- There are no rules on `medical_profiles`, `contacts`, or `registrations` rows themselves.

Two new pieces of infrastructure code:

- `DirectusPolicy`, a resource for an extra policy attached to a role.
- `presets` support on `DirectusPermissionRule`.

The Guardian role stays unused.

**Directus staff move to the `authentik` provider.** Directus usernames are unique emails. A
staff member who is also a parent would collide with the Community user that the `authentik`
provider tries to create, and the Directus login would fail. The move is one change to
`ungoodUser` (`directus-roles.ts:62-68`). `google` stays enabled until that login is verified.
The bootstrap admin password is the break-glass path.

### Opt-in: newest answer wins

`share_contact` sits on the participant row. `promoted_fields` writes the registration's person,
so the Clubspot answer lands there.

- **Portal.** One family toggle updates every participant the viewer is a guardian of. An adult
  participant can also update their own row. The preset stamps `share_contact_updated_at`.
- **Clubspot, from Spring.** The time of an answer is its registration's `registered_at`.
  `custom_field_responses` has no timestamp of its own. `planPromotedFields` gets a newest-wins
  mode for this one target. It writes `share_contact`, and it writes `registered_at` into
  `share_contact_updated_at`, when the winning response is newer than the stored timestamp or the
  stored timestamp is null. It parses Yes and No explicitly, and it counts and logs any other
  answer. `PROMOTABLE_PERSON_FIELDS` (`packages/clubspot/src/promoted-fields.ts:7`) allows text
  only today.
- An answer edited in Clubspot after registration keeps the old `registered_at`, so the sync
  ignores the edit.

### Authentik deployment

- **Containers.** `authentik-server` and `authentik-worker`, with a Caddy block for `login.`. Pin
  a release that needs no Redis.
- **Database.** `postgres.database("authentik")` and a user
  (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/database.ts:122-141`). `db-g1-small` allows about
  50 connections. Cap Authentik's workers and connection age so that it and Directus fit.
- **Memory.** The VM is `e2-medium` with 4 GB (`compute.ts:11`). Authentik wants about 2 GB. The
  implementer measures `docker stats` and **stops to report the numbers before adding Authentik**.
  The user then compares a resize with other hosting options, such as GKE Autopilot.
- **Secrets.** Pulumi's `randomSecret` in `infrastructure` makes the bootstrap token, the secret
  key, the DB password, and the Directus OIDC client secret. They are granted to `substrate-runner`.
- **Config.** A new Pulumi project, `packages/infrastructure/src/authentik`, applied after
  `infrastructure`. It uses the goauthentik Terraform provider through
  `pulumi package add terraform-provider`, wrapped in classes with secure defaults. It declares:
  - the Google source, with email matching
  - the email-code flow and SMTP
  - the proxy application for `cycsail.team`
  - the Directus OIDC application and its lowercasing scope mapping
  - the `staff` and `families` groups
  - "users cannot change their own email"
  - the sync's service account, whose RBAC role covers creating users and managing those two
    groups only

  It reads the Directus client secret by name, as `crm/index.ts:37-41` reads the admin password.
- **IAM.** The job's service account goes in `packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap`, like
  `gsuite-sync.ts`. Its grants go in `config.ts`. It needs domain-wide delegation for
  `admin.directory.group.member.readonly`, which is a manual Workspace step. Its Directus machine
  user gets:
  - read on `people` (`id`, `email`) and update on `people` (`login_email`) only
  - read on `contacts`, `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `camps`, and `programs`
  - read and update on `classes`, where the update is limited to `roster_current`
- **Retire oauth2-proxy.** Remove its container, `portalOauthCookieSecret` (`portal.ts:220-224`),
  and `substrateSelfSign` (`substrate.ts:32-36`). `substrateSelfSign` exists only for oauth2-proxy's
  delegation. Revoke the substrate account's delegation in Workspace.

### Email

Authentik sends as `noreply@cyccommunitysailing.org` through the Workspace SMTP relay. The relay
authenticates the VM's static IP (`compute.ts:24`). Before any code is emailed, fix DNS at the
registrar:

1. Merge the SPF records into one:
   `v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com ~all`.
2. Turn on Workspace DKIM, and publish its key.
3. Delete the stray `v=DMARC1` TXT record at the apex. `_dmarc` already holds the real one.

### Production verification

The rules are license-gated, and `dev/directus-local` runs without a license
(`dev/directus-local/docker-compose.yml:10`). They are checked in production against a hidden
Clubspot test camp. Its classes map to test programs P and Q, and one class in P belongs to an
ended camp.

| Login               | Setup                                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `a@` (lowercase)    | Guardian of minor A1 in P, opted in. A1 shares `a@`.                                   |
| `b@`                | Clubspot holds it as `B@`. Guardian of minor B1 in P. `share_contact` is null.         |
| `c@`                | Adult participant in P, opted in.                                                     |
| `d@`                | Participant in P with no date of birth, opted in.                                     |
| `e@`                | Guardian of E1 in Q, opted in.                                                        |
| `i@`                | Guardian of I1, who is only in P's ended-camp class, opted in.                        |
| `x@`                | No match.                                                                             |
| a staff account     | A member of `all@`.                                                                   |

Expected results through the REST API as each login:

- [ ] `a@` reads names A1, B1, C, D. It reads no E1 and no I1.
- [ ] `a@` reads email and phone for A and C only. It reads B's row not at all, and it reads no
      email for A1, B1, or D.
- [ ] `b@` sees the same names, and contact for A and C. This proves the case normalization.
- [ ] `e@` reads E1 only. `i@` reads nothing in P.
- [ ] `x@` gets the help page, and `/items/people` returns an empty list.
- [ ] `a@` PATCHes A1 `share_contact` to false. `b@` loses A's contact on its next read.
      `share_contact_updated_at` holds server time, even when the payload sends another value.
- [ ] `a@` cannot PATCH B1, or A1's `email`. `d@` cannot PATCH anything, because it is not Adult.
- [ ] `c@` can PATCH its own `share_contact`.
- [ ] Every Community login gets 403 or an empty list from `medical_profiles`, `contacts`, and
      `registrations`.
- [ ] Staff see the staff sections, and they still have Staff rights in the Data Studio.
- [ ] Record the response time of the roster query. The teammate filter is about ten relations
      deep.

### Launch prerequisite

The board must approve sharing names and contact information before the `families` pass is turned
on. Everything else ships and is verified with test accounts before that approval.

### Future work

- Finer staff sections, and roles from #156, replacing the `all@` mirror.
